cards.title: Allometric Scaling Method Selection and Species Constraints
cards.claim: Human clearance prediction by allometry requires a specified species set, scaling method and exponent. In the cited dataset, single-species optimal exponents were 0.65-0.70 for small molecules and 0.75-0.80 for macromolecules; monkey liver-blood-flow scaling had AFE <= 2.0 in that analysis. In that dataset, renal small-molecule simple allometry had lower average error than hepatic small-molecule scaling, especially at low extraction; MLP/BRW corrections reduced some group-level errors. These observations do not fix a default exponent or guarantee a target-drug prediction.
conditions: Applicable when animal PK data is qualified and body weights are available.
Do not pool CL/F with absolute CL or Vz with Vss.
Count unique qualified species, not duplicate publications.
required_inputs: Qualified animal clearance estimates (CL) with provenance.
Body weights for all species used in scaling.
Explicit method specification (e.g., simple allometry, LBF, ROE).
limitations: No universal minimum species count is established.
Prediction error is high for low hepatic extraction ratio drugs using simple allometry.
A good animal regression fit does not validate human prediction accuracy.
cards.downstream_use: Generates prospective human clearance scenarios for dose prediction.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
